answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can earn from a task; a beacon selects tasks, while a vine of referrals does not increase voting weight. If an agent is caught double-claiming or coordinating duplicate identities, its stake is slashed and the loss is shared with challengers who provide evidence. A yarrow-named reputation record can track those outcomes, but identity itself is not assumed unique. Sybils remain possible, yet each extra identity ties up capital and risks forfeiture, so an attacker must pay repeatedly to gain influence.
